correctness.rationale: The two normalized Pauli terms anticommute and are traceless; Q is a traceless involution, with two eigenvalues of each sign. Their commutators with H cancel with the stated coefficients, and Q commutes with charger Z. For either L or its Hilbert–Schmidt adjoint the dissipation is −γ‖[Z_C,A]‖₂²/8, forcing every fixed or imaginary-axis eigenoperator to be charger-block-diagonal. The block equations then identify the kernel with the commutant of TT†, where T=F I+gσ⁻ and det T=F²; TT† has distinct eigenvalues since g>0. The commutant is two-dimensional and I,Q span it. The Hamiltonian sends a charger-block-diagonal operator to the off-diagonal blocks under commutation, so no nonzero imaginary eigenvalue survives. Hilbert–Schmidt contraction from the same dissipation identity excludes Jordan blocks on the axis. The limit is the orthogonal projection onto the common adjoint and Schrödinger kernel, giving (I+Tr(Qρ)Q)/4 on states and the stated binary measure-and-prepare formula. This is entanglement breaking against an external reference; its outputs are also classical on the charger. The two conditional battery vectors have common X component 2Fc/s and opposite Z components ∓gc/s, with s=√(g²+4F²). For nonzero c they are not collinear and the density matrices cannot share a battery eigenbasis; this gives precisely the directional discord claim. The reduced battery has zero Z component and Bloch length 2F|c|/s, and its passive energy is ω_B(1−2F|c|/s)/2. Taking c=±1 proves sharpness and the joint ground state gives c=−g/s in the declared convention. The proof is in the rotating frame and concerns limiting, not finite-time, entanglement breaking. value.rationale: The asymptotic map answers which preparation information survives even with correlations and an arbitrary external reference. It cleanly distinguishes elimination of entanglement from survival of battery-side discord, and gives a sharp continuum of accessible work at identical final mean energy. This is a complete answer to a natural exact model question beyond the known ground-state charging benchmark. It invokes no new general channel principle and makes no claim of a free preparation advantage.
